title: Family of four, toddler, 2h, Rs 7200, rain, step-free, Colaba hotel
why: The PS's own example. This one scenario exercises the isochrone, the duration gate, the budget gate, the compound access need, the weather gate, the category-diversity rule and the walk-in availability gate simultaneously. If it passes, the pipeline works.

notes.durationGate: Total travel plus activity plus buffer must fit inside 120 minutes. Most Colaba records are 35-50 minutes plus 8-12 minutes of travel, so two stops is the realistic ceiling and three only if both are short.
notes.accessibility: `wheelchair` is the hard one. A `stepFree: false` record must be rejected with `not_step_free` and never softened. `restroom` is a separate check and only 40 of 133 records claim a toilet on site, which is the honest state of the city and exactly what the unmet-demand feed exists to surface.
notes.budget: 720000 paise for four people is Rs 1800 per head, which is what two sit-down stops in Colaba actually cost. The two cheapest records that are step-free AND have a toilet on site are Cafe Tulip at Rs 800 and Cafe Mondegar at Rs 900, so Rs 1700 per head is the real floor. Britannia at Rs 2200 per head does not fit, and the budget gate is what says so.

title: Solo backpacker, six hours, no constraints, Colaba
why: Cold start with a wide window. The hard requirement is diversity: a six-hour window can trivially absorb six restaurants, and returning six restaurants is the failure mode a ranking engine falls into. `maxSameCategory: 2` is what catches it.

notes.categoryDiversity: 26 categories are available and 21 are in use. A six-hour solo plan should draw from at least four of them.
notes.walkMode: `travelMode: walk` should keep legs under about 1.2 km and total walking under 4 km for the day. Anything further needs a surfaced alternative.

title: Forty-five minutes, nothing booked, on a Colaba pavement
why: A tiny window must still return something. This is the graceful-degradation test: the packer has to fall to the `single_best` rung rather than return an empty plan and a shrug. The 15-minute Wadia Clock Tower and the 20-minute Bademeir exist in the catalogue specifically so this scenario can pass.

notes.rungs: Expect `single_best` here. The plan is allowed to be one stop, and that is not a failure. What IS a failure is returning a 90-minute record in a 45-minute window.

title: Rs 0. Just a walk somewhere nice, ninety minutes
why: Zero budget must mean genuinely zero, not nearly zero. 74 of 133 records have `pricePerPerson: null`, so this should be the easiest scenario in the suite to satisfy, and if it fails then the budget gate is broken rather than the data being thin.

notes.budgetGate: A total budget of 0 means any positive `pricePerPerson` is rejected with `over_budget` and a shortfall in paise. That is the number the message should quote.

title: Eight hours, nothing excluded, Bandra start
why: The upper bound. The failure mode here is over-planning: a packer that has eight hours and 40 feasible records will happily hand back eleven stops and a twelve-hour day. `maxStops: 5` plus a stress-score ceiling is the test.

notes.overPlanning: `Plan.totalMin` must never exceed `availableMin`, even on the `greedy_fill` rung. If it does, the validator should catch it as a violation rather than the UI hiding it.

title: Two adults, no children, somewhere quiet, ninety minutes, Fort
why: A negative-only request. There is no `pos` at all, which is the case ITINERA's own decomposition does not handle well. The engine has to score purely on the penalty channel and still return something. `requireCalmStop` asks for at least one stop whose `perception.atmosphere` contains a solitude-ish term.

notes.negativeChannel: `neg` is a first-class field in the contract and must be applied as a penalty against the retrieval candidates, not used to filter a pre-scored list. Both are wrong in different ways; the penalty is the one that can be explained to a user.

title: Wheelchair user, 90 minutes, monsoon, Bandra
why: The compound case. `not_step_free` must be a hard kill, and a heavy-rain context must additionally drop the outdoor records. `ban-movietown` is deliberately `stepFree: true` in the data and still forbidden, so the engine has to find a real reason or the scenario is measuring the wrong thing — see the `forbiddenBecause` note.

notes.falseNegatives: docs/DATA_SPEC.md §4 is explicit that a false negative is worse than a false positive here, because a wheelchair user is stranded. That is why 95 records are `stepFree: true`, 38 are `false` and none are `null`, and why `hearingLoop` is 120/7/3 null/true/false instead.

title: Stroller, three hours, uneven ground, Marine Drive
why: `strollerOk` is a separate 3-state field from `stepFree` in the contract, and conflating them is the most common accessibility bug. Ten records are `strollerOk: null` and the gate must treat null as unknown, not as yes.

notes.nullHandling: `md-riverfront-evening` is `strollerOk: true` in the data and one review says the paving has washed out. That is a genuine disagreement between the curated field and the review signal, and it is the kind of thing the `bestTimeOfDay` correction loop exists to catch. The gate should still pass it; the review signal should surface as a caveat.

title: Older adult, low stairs and a hearing loop, two hours, Fort
why: The rare compound need. `no_hearing_loop` must be an exact-match failure: `hearingLoop: null` is unknown, and unknown is not a pass for a hard access need. Only 7 records claim a hearing loop, and two of them are explicitly curated `false` (unamplified organs), so the engine has exactly five real options and that is the honest state of the data.

notes.knownLimitation: Every one of the five `hearingLoop: true` records is `inferred` at confidence below 1, because we have not surveyed any of them. The UI must show that badge. This is the weakest honest part of the catalogue and it should be said out loud in the demo rather than hidden.

title: Someone who needs a toilet within the hour, 60 minutes, Bandra
why: The single most common unmet need and the least glamorous. 93 of 133 records have `restroomOnSite: false`, all of them curated rather than guessed, which is why the provider opportunity feed has something true to say: there is no public toilet on the Bandra seafront and there never will be.

notes.unmetDemand: When this scenario runs, the `UnmetDemand` row should show `topBlockingCode: no_restroom` and a count close to 30. That is the provider-side demo beat, and it is the strongest argument in the product that the data is honest.

title: Jain vegetarian, lunch window 12:30 to 14:00 exactly, near a temple
why: A narrow meal window with a hard diet filter. The visit interval must sit entirely inside the venue's open interval, and `diets` is an open vocabulary in the contract precisely because iD's cuisine list omits mughlai, maharashtrian and chaat — all of which are load-bearing here. `visitWindowInsideOpeningHours` is the assertion that catches an off-by-one on the 90-minute window.

notes.dietSemantics: `diet_mismatch` is the right code for a market or a bar, but it is the WRONG code for a venue that simply does not declare a jain option. Those are different failures and the distinction shows up in the unmet-demand feed: the first is a cuisine problem, the second is a missing field. A v2 refinement, not a v1 bug.

title: Teen 16 and grandparent 70, three hours, one wants to walk, one wants shade
why: Group tension made visible rather than averaged. `docs/EVAL_SPEC.md` §9 predicts this scenario will be the weakest in the suite, and that prediction is recorded before running it rather than after. The assertion is not that the plan is good but that at least one stop genuinely serves both halves of the party and the disagreement is named in the output.

notes.knownRisky: Shared constraints plus per-person personas exist; negotiation does not. Expect a compromise and expect the tension axis to be thin. Report it.

title: Three adults, one Jain, Rs 900 total, two hours, Bandra
why: Party size times diet times budget together. Rs 900 for three people is Rs 300 a head, which rules out every sit-down restaurant in the catalogue and leaves the street, the sweet shop and the covered market. The diet filter narrows that further, and the combination is the test.

notes.interactionOrder: The gate order in docs/DATA_SPEC.md matters here. If budget is checked before capacity and before diet, the rejection message names the wrong constraint and the why-ledger is misleading even though the outcome is right.

title: Business traveller, 40 minutes between meetings, 17:20

origin.label: Fort, near the Bombay Stock Exchange

why: Extreme tightness at an awkward hour, and the one that catches the opening-hours adapter. At 17:20 on a weekday, Novelty Theatre is between matinee and evening, Dongri to Dubai has shut, and the Causeway market has finished for the day. Only 15-40 minute records survive, which is exactly why the catalogue carries a 15-minute record.

notes.hoursAdapter: `hours.raw` values here are `Mo-Sa 10:00-19:00` and `Mo-Sa 18:00-21:00`. The adapter must return `open: false` for the former at 1040 only if the raw string is wrong — it is not, the market genuinely closes at 19:00, so 17:20 should PASS. Recheck the forbidden list: Causeway market is open until 21:00 and must not be forbidden on hours. Move it to acceptableIds or drop the assertion.

title: 23:00, two hours, night market and live music, Colaba
why: The day-boundary case. `nowMin` of 1380 is 23:00 and a 120-minute window crosses midnight, so the engine has to handle minutes-from-midnight arithmetic wrapping past 1440 rather than producing a negative window. `col-leopold-cafe` is open until 01:00 and `col-chaat-mile-marker` until 23:30, and both are the reason this is satisfiable.

notes.clockWrap: If `Minutes` is a plain 0..1440 integer, a plan that starts at 23:30 and ends at 00:30 needs a documented rule. Either the clock is local-day-relative and endMin wraps, or the context carries a date. The contract allows neither today, so the engine needs a stated convention and this scenario is where it shows.

title: 06:00, shift worker, two hours, Fort
why: Early morning, when almost everything is shut, and the test is graceful degradation rather than coverage. The honest answer at 06:00 is a chai counter, a 24/7 fountain, an open lawn and a tiffin carrier. All four exist in the catalogue because this scenario is why they were written.

notes.kissaHours: `fort-kissa-corner` carries `hours.status: absent` with a `Mo-Sa 07:30-20:00` string, so it is 90 minutes from opening and must be rejected on `hours_unverified` rather than optimistically accepted. It is listed as acceptable here on the understanding that the gate either rejects it (correct) or accepts it (a bug worth catching). If the suite passes either way the assertion is too weak — tighten to require at least one stop.

title: Lunch 12:30 to 14:00 exactly, Rs 1200 for two, Bandra
why: Opening-hours window precision with a meal placement. `ban-goan-kitchen` opens at 12:30, so a 12:30 arrival is exactly at the boundary and a 13:00 arrival is comfortably inside. An off-by-one in the adapter is invisible until this scenario runs.

notes.boundaryAtOpen: Several `hours.raw` values use the multi-range form `Mo-Su 12:30-15:00,19:00-22:30`. The `opening_hours` npm port handles multi-range correctly but does NOT support `PH off` or inline comments, which is why two records in the catalogue carry deliberately unparsable strings.

title: A place with unparsable hours is requested explicitly
why: The must-see path with messy hours. `col-sassoon-steps-sketch` has clean hours but `not_step_free`, and `fort-basement-gallery`, `md-print-room-lantern` and `col-farsi-reading-room` carry `status: unparsable`. The required behaviour is not a crash and not a silent pass: it is `hours_unverified`, a visible badge, and either a pass with the badge or a rejection with a finished message.
notes: The harness must not 500. There are three `absent` and three `unparsable` records in the catalogue, so this is exercised by ordinary retrieval, not only by an explicit request.

title: Heavy rain, three hours, Rs 1200, Colaba
why: The weather gate at its strongest. `indoorOutdoor: outdoor` plus `weatherSensitive: any|rain` plus a `heavy_rain` context must kill the record. Note that `col-gateway-of-india` is `weatherSensitive: any` and is a 45-minute flat open plaza, so if the engine keeps it the rejection must be a real written reason rather than a shrug.

notes.coveredSurvives: `col-cafe-tulip` is `covered` and `col-monsoon-film-walk` is `covered` and both survive. That is the entire reason the `covered` member of the enum exists and the reason the catalogue has five of them.

title: Heat wave, 11:00 to 16:00, two hours, no budget
why: `weatherSensitive: heat` is the other half of the weather gate and the one most engines forget. Seven records carry it and the Hanging Gardens record explicitly says it is unusable at midday. The pair is `older_adults` with `lowStairs`, which removes most of the outdoor options anyway, so this scenario mostly tests that the two filters compose rather than fight.
notes: `lowStairsAlias()` in the raw line above is a placeholder mistake and must be the literal `["lowStairs"]`. Fixing it here in the file rather than in prose is the point of having a validator.

title: Navi Mumbai CBD to South Mumbai, two hours, transit only

origin.label: Navi Mumbai CBD, near the railway station

why: Documented in advance as a known weakness. The catalogue has 133 records and none of them are in Navi Mumbai, and the committed isochrone data covers only Bandra West and Pali Hill. The correct behaviour is `expectCoverage: false` with a clean, explained zero and a populated `UnmetDemand` row. If the engine returns a South Mumbai plan with fabricated travel times, that is a serious bug and this scenario is the thing that catches it.
notes: Predicted before running, per docs/EVAL_SPEC.md §9. `CITY_MANIFEST.transitCorridors` is hand-seeded for the Western, Central, Harbour and Metro lines, and a Navi-to-South journey is exactly the case where a hand-seeded table has gaps.

title: Bandra to Colaba, one hour, peak hour, car
why: The Mumbai reality check. Bandra to Colaba is 21 minutes by train and 38 by car in traffic, and free-flow routing understates peak by three to five times. `minReportedTravelRatio: 2.0` asserts that any reported car travel time is at least twice the straight-line distance at peak, which is the cheapest possible guard against a hardcoded free-flow number.
notes: Every leg must be labelled `estimated: true`. If any leg reports `estimated: false` without a live routing result behind it, that is the failure docs/DATA_SPEC.md warns about.

title: Origin is a residential lane, not a landmark

origin.label: 3rd Floor, Sunbeam Apartments, off Hill Road, Bandra West

why: Geocoding fallback. `origin.point` is null and the label is an address a traveller would actually type. The engine has to fall back to something sensible and say what it did rather than treating the point as (0,0) off the coast of Africa. The subtle failure is a null point silently becoming a valid GeoPoint, which is why this is in the suite at all.
notes: If geocoding is unavailable offline, the correct fallback is a neighbourhood centroid with a visible 'approximate start location' caveat and a slightly wider travel-time margin, not a crash and not a silent zero.

title: I don't want tourists

origin.label: Colaba, back lane behind the Causeway

why: Negative-only again, and the no-tourists version is a genuine signal rather than a synonym for quiet. It maps to the local-authenticity scoring component and to `review.partyType` distribution: a record whose reviews are all `partyType: family_with_children` at a Sunday market reads as tourist-facing even though nothing about it says so.
notes: `notInTopTenTouristList` needs a concrete list, and docs/FEATURES.md or the harness should own it. Without one this assertion is decorative. Flagged rather than papered over.

title: Something local, not a chain, two hours, Colaba
why: The demo script's typed line, so it needs to work. Negation is `chains` and the positive request is `local food`, which is the realistic shape of how people ask. `col-britannia-co` and `col-chaat-mile-marker` are the two obvious answers and a plan that misses both has got the negative channel wrong.
notes: `col-leopold-cafe` is forbidden here and allowed in the `couple-wants-alone` scenario's context only in the sense that it was not in its acceptable set. Its own review says unapologetically tourist-facing, which is the signal the authenticity component should read.

title: Plan built, then ninety minutes lost

change.narrative: You have lost ninety minutes, so you now have about ninety.

why: Adaptive replanning, the case the PS asks for by name. The replanner must diff against `original` (180 minutes), not against the mutated 90, and it must drop the tail rather than rebuild from scratch. Two swaps is the target and the demo metric.
notes: `expectKeptIntentTerms` is the important one. A replan that returns three cafes has preserved the mechanics and lost the intent, and `preservedIntent: true` on its own would not catch that.

title: Plan built, then it starts raining
why: The replanner's marquee case, and the second beat of the demo script. Every outdoor stop should be replaced by a covered or indoor one within two swaps, and the intent (`sea`) must survive the swap even though the venue changed. `md-monsoon-seawall` is `covered` precisely so this has a landing place.
notes: `md-grand-hotel-seaview` is a real venue with a covered terrace, so it is both the right answer and a slightly awkward one: the product recommending a hotel cafe is honest but not charming. Better to name the covered arcade first.

title: First stop sells out mid-session

change.narrative: The gallery is full; they will not take more people tonight.

why: The hardest of the three replans, and the one where a naive implementation rebuilds the whole plan. The rest of the plan must be pinned and survive untouched; only the sold-out stop is replaced, and the replacement must not duplicate a pinned stop. One swap, not two.
notes: `fort-basement-gallery` holds thirty and roughly seventy people turn up on an opening night, per one of its own reviews. That is the concrete evidence for a `sold_out` rejection rather than a hypothetical one.

title: The traveller types something we cannot parse
rawInput: ummm so like maybe something cool?? idk not the crowded tourist stuff, my friend wants to see that thing with the boats though. no rush we have like 2 hrs i think??
why: Vague, hedged, self-contradicting input. The traveller says no rush and then two hours, mentions boats and does not say they want to actually go on one, and asks for nothing specific. `mustNotInventConstraints` is the assertion that matters: the NLU may not silently add `accessNeeds` or `diets` that nobody said. It may propose, it may not apply.
notes: This is the scenario that justifies the LLM at all. With `LLM=off` the deterministic regex parser should still return a plan, just a plainer one, and the two plans should be compared in EVAL_RESULTS.md as a cost-quality table.

title: The model is down mid-session
why: The credibility anchor, and the fifth beat of the demo script. With the model down, the engine must produce the same constraint satisfaction and the same rejections. What it loses is narrative quality, not correctness. If this scenario needs the model to pass, the architecture is wrong and docs/EVAL_SPEC.md says so in advance.
notes: `allRejectionsHaveFinishedMessages` is the assertion that actually tests the thesis. Every `Rejection.message` must be a finished sentence with a real number in it, and a placeholder there is the single clearest sign that the feature is decorative.

title: Something local and not touristy, two hours, Fort, no named place

origin.label: Fort, near the Wadia Clock Tower

requests.neg: tourists, queues, being asked to buy anything

why: The authenticity scenario with a real constraint attached, which makes it more than a taste question. The catalogue has 17 `hidden_place` records, several of them explicitly negative in their own `perception.atmosphere` so the crowd and authenticity penalties have real material rather than nothing to work with.
notes: `adj-kala-ghoda-vernacular-walk` is the strongest answer in the whole catalogue for this and it is a synthetic record, which is a thing to be honest about: the real Fort back lanes exist and are the right answer, and the walk that names them is ours.
